_about: Open building-footprint polygon sources for the ADU setback engine's 28 jurisdictions (6 counties). Every record marked verified=true was exercised with a live request on 2026-10-18 from this machine; status + feature counts are recorded as returned. Records with verified=false were found in catalogs/search only. Mirrors the style of gaudi-api-port/services/parcel_data/county_registry.py: keyless ArcGIS REST /query layers, per-source quirks surfaced so the engine can flag them.

query_convention.arcgis_parcel_polygon: POST {layer_url}/query with geometry=<esri polygon json of the parcel>&geometryType=esriGeometryPolygon&inSR=4326&spatialRel=esriSpatialRelIntersects&outFields=*&outSR=4326&f=geojson  -- preferred: returns every structure touching the lot in one call; clip each result to the parcel before picking the primary house.
query_convention.notes: All ArcGIS layers below report errors in-band with HTTP 200 (check payload.error), exactly like the parcel fabrics. Test bboxes are +/-0.001 deg (~100 m x ~90 m) around the test point.

sources.name: San Mateo County - Building Footprints
sources.format: ArcGIS REST (f=geojson supported); daily S3 exports in SHP/GDB/KML/GeoJSON
sources.license: Not stated on the item (licenseInfo empty); published as county open data on the SMC Hub. Treat as county open data, attribution 'San Mateo County GIS'.
sources.vintage: Not documented on the service (description empty, LASTUPDATE null on all rows). Menlo Park's own service credits its county-sourced footprints to 'San Mateo County GIS (LiDAR) 2020', so the base capture is most likely the 2020 countywide LiDAR; the layer is edited continuously (dataLastEditDate 2026-10-18, exported daily per the download page).

attributes.height: BLDGHEIGHT (ft, populated; 15 in sample), BASEELEV, EAVEHEIGHT (null in sample)
attributes.building_type: FEATURECODE exists but every row is null

quirks: No main/accessory flag and no APN: pick the primary house by largest clipped-area polygon on the parcel.
LiDAR-derived outlines are roof extents (eaves), not wall lines - over-states the footprint by roughly the eave overhang.

Sibling layer 'Buildings' (https://services.arcgis.com/yq3FgOI44hYHAFVZ/arcgis/rest/services/Buildings/FeatureServer/0, static 2022-02-25 snapshot, metadata-only check) carries APN, OutBuild flag, BUILD_TYPE and assessor situs joined onto each footprint - useful as a one-time lookup for main-vs-outbuilding, but it is frozen at 2022.
Sibling 'Building_Footprint_Elevations' (2023-12-06) adds MIN_/MAX_/MEAN elevation; not needed.

sources.name: Santa Clara County - Building Outlines (2022 LiDAR)

alternates.2020_lidar_hub_layer: https://maps.santaclaracounty.gov/server/rest/services/opendata/SCCGISHUB/MapServer/40  (Buildings Footprints 2D, early-2020 LiDAR, maxRecordCount 5000; verified 200 / 29 features at Palo Alto)

sources.format: ArcGIS REST MapServer layer (Map,Query,Data; f=geojson supported)
sources.license: County of Santa Clara open data; copyrightText 'County of Santa Clara; Sanborn Map Co.'
sources.vintage: LiDAR collected late 2022 (Sanborn, 0.35 m NPS, USGS base spec); 2D footprints from Class-6 building returns. Heights interpolated DSM-DEM.
sources.last_updated: 2022 capture; service has no editingInfo (static deliverable)

attributes.height: Building_H (ft, rooftop above base), Base_Heigh (base elevation ft)
attributes.building_type: Class exists but every row null

quirks: Polygons are 'based on rooftop area, not building base area' (county metadata) - same eave caveat as SMC.

Same bbox returns 22 (2022 layer) vs 29 (2020 layer) features: the 2022 product appears to merge/suppress small structures more aggressively. If a detached garage is missing, cross-check the 2020 layer.
No main/accessory flag; use area-on-parcel heuristic.

sources.name: Marin County - Building Footprints (MarinMap)
sources.license: County of Marin 'as is' disclaimer (no reuse restriction stated); open data item owner opendata_MarinCounty.
sources.vintage: Stereo-compiled from the 2004 orthophoto project (urban/suburban extent + 200 ft fringe); additions digitized from 2014 orthophoto, 2018 imagery and city 'Building Plan' sources (SourceCode/SourceDateYear per feature). Sample at Mill Valley: SourceCode 'Vargis_2004 10cm', SourceDateYear 2004.

attributes.building_type: BuildingType coded domain: 1 General/Residential, 2 Government, 3 Medical, 4 Education, 5 Transportation, 6 Commercial, 7 Religious, 8 Recreation, 9 Cultural/Heritage, 10 Hospitality, 11 Airport, 12 Industrial, 13 CommunityCenter

quirks: Oldest county source in the set (2004 base). Houses rebuilt/expanded after 2004-2014 may be wrong; use SourceDateYear to decide whether to prefer Overture/Microsoft for that parcel.
Stereo-compiled at the ground base, so these ARE wall footprints (not roof extents) - unlike the LiDAR counties.
Coverage limited to the urban/suburban mapping extent (fine for the three towns).

sources.name: Contra Costa County - no published building footprint layer

verified.notes: Enumerated https://gis.cccounty.us/arcgis/rest/services (folders _Authoritative, AUTHORATIVE/BASE_DATA_DCD_ArcPro, INTERNET/BASE_DATA_ArcPro, CCMAP, Hosted, RASTER...): address points, parcels, zoning, contours, 2019/2025 imagery - no buildings layer. ArcGIS Online catalog search for county-owned 'building footprints' returned 0 Contra Costa results; Lafayette/Moraga/Orinda returned 0.

quirks: Use the global baseline here: Overture (verified 11 features at Lafayette, all sourced from Microsoft ML Buildings, every one with a height) or the Microsoft GlobalML tile for quadkey 023010212.
Older academic snapshots exist (DCD 'building outlines of schools' etc. via Berkeley GeoData) but nothing residential/countywide.

sources.name: Sonoma County - Buildings (BASEPublic)

alternates.owts_copy: https://socogis.sonomacounty.ca.gov/map/rest/services/OWTSPublic/Buildings/FeatureServer/0 (same data, same host as the parcel fabric already in county_registry)

sources.license: County GIS public services (no license text on the layer); same terms as the Cities_GIS_Parcel_Base fabric the engine already uses.
sources.vintage: Countywide outlines originally from 2000 1-ft orthophotography; cities of Sonoma and Healdsburg added later; maintained since - item metadata says outlines were updated from the EagleView May-2025 orthophoto capture. Sample at Healdsburg last_edited_date 2025-11-04. Only structures >= 150 sq ft are captured.

attributes.building_type: PropType: Single Family Residence, Attached Unit Residence, Condominium Residence, Multiple Family Residence, Mobile Home, Out Building, Commercial, Industrial, Agriculture, Government, School, Park Building, Parking Structure, Solar Panel, ...
attributes.main_vs_accessory: partial - PropType 'Out Building' marks accessory structures; the house is the 'Single Family Residence' polygon

quirks: Structures under 150 sq ft are absent (small sheds) - irrelevant for the primary house, relevant for separation checks.

Where 2000-era imagery was coarser than 1 ft/px the original capture was a point converted to a 36 sq ft square; those should have been replaced by the 2025 update but treat near-square ~36 sq ft polygons as placeholders.
PropType is null on many rows; fall back to the area heuristic when it is.

sources.name: Napa County - BuildingFootprint_Public

alternates.county_server_copy: https://gis.napacounty.gov/arcgis/rest/services/Hosted/Building_Footprints_Public/FeatureServer/0 (metadata verified: same data, lastEditDate 2026-10-16, maxRecordCount 1000, supports Sync/Extract)
alternates.legacy_host: https://gis.countyofnapa.org/... - TLS certificate expired; do not use

sources.license: Open Data Commons Public Domain Dedication and License (PDDL) v1.0 - stated on the AGOL item.
sources.vintage: Maintained local-government footprint layer (ortho/aerial compiled; the 2014 public snapshot warned coverage was incomplete). Synced weekly to AGOL; sample feature last_edited_date 2022-06-08.

attributes.building_type: FEATURECODE: Addressed Building, Addressed Structure, Non-Addressed Building, Non-Addressed Structure, Non-Address Structure, Outbuilding, Water Tower (+ typo variants 'Addressed Buildicng', 'Outbuiclding', 'Outbuildng')
attributes.main_vs_accessory: partial - 'Addressed Building' is the house; 'Outbuilding' / 'Non-Addressed *' are accessory
attributes.apn_or_address: Parcel (APN; comma-separated list when a building spans parcels), Address (comma list), Municipality, Community

quirks: FEATURECODE values contain typos - match with startswith('Addressed Building') / startswith('Outbuild') rather than equality.
Parcel field can hold several APNs; split on ', ' before matching to the subject parcel.
Height/stories columns exist but are zero-filled.

sources.name: City of Palo Alto - Building Roof Outline
sources.portal_url: https://palo-alto.maps.arcgis.com/ (ArcGIS Online org evmyRZRrsopdeog7; Open GIS program)
sources.license: Not stated on the service; City of Palo Alto Open GIS data (public).
sources.vintage: Heads-up digitized from city orthos (SOURCE values: Photo 1999/2001/2004/2006/2013, Accela permits, field obs...). Sample feature SOURCE 'Photo 2013', MODIFIEDDATE 2020-10-06. Service still edited (dataLastEditDate 2026-08-10).

attributes.other: SOURCE, INPUTMETHOD, JURISDICTION (PA/...), CALCULATEDAREA (sq ft), OWNER/NAME for public buildings

quirks: It is explicitly a ROOF outline (includes eaves) - subtract the eave overhang before measuring wall setbacks, or use the county LiDAR layer for geometry and this layer only for the major/minor flag.
Per-feature vintage varies widely (1993-2013 photos); check SOURCE/MODIFIEDDATE.

sources.name: City of Sunnyvale - Building Footprints
sources.portal_url: https://gis.sunnyvale.ca.gov/ (AGOL org IBwZaktrBtZuqQmg, item owner Vestra_CityofSunnyvale)
sources.license: Not stated on the service (public item).
sources.vintage: Not documented; attributes (BLDG_HIGH/BLDG_LOW elevations) indicate a LiDAR/photogrammetric capture. Item created 2021-06-02; data last edited 2023-08-13.

attributes.building_type: BLDG_TYPE: Main, Dwelling, Accessory(<100), Accessory(100-700), Accessory(>700), Parking, Structure(<7), Merged APNs
attributes.main_vs_accessory: yes - BLDG_TYPE 'Main' (or 'Dwelling'); Accessory(...) buckets by sq ft
attributes.apn_or_address: APN, APNNUM, Address, SiteNumber, BuildingNumber, UNIT

quirks: Richest schema in the survey (APN + Main/Accessory + stories + height). Prefer it over the county layer for Sunnyvale.
APN is stored without dashes (e.g. 20929054); normalize before joining to the county parcel fabric.
Published by a consultant account (Vestra); not an official hub item - re-check availability periodically.

sources.name: City of Menlo Park - Buildings (GISWeb)
sources.format: ArcGIS REST MapServer layer 3 'Buildings' (Map,Query,Data; f=geojson supported). Layer 0 is facility points - do not use.
sources.license: Not stated; city public map service.
sources.vintage: Mixed per service description: digitized from orthos ca. 2015, Belle Haven planimetric survey ca. 2000, San Mateo County GIS LiDAR 2020. Sample feature RevDate 2024-06-27.

attributes.building_type: BldgType 1-4 (coded, no domain published) + BldgSubType free text (Garage, Carport, Apartment, Condo, Office, Church, School, ...)
attributes.main_vs_accessory: partial - BldgSubType 'Garage'/'Carport' flags accessory; residential mains are usually null subtype

quirks: Largely the same 2020 county LiDAR geometry with city edits; use it for Address/Stories/Garage tags, county layer for consistency.
BldgType codes are undocumented (values 1-4).

sources.name: City of San Mateo - Building_Footprints_Zoning (layer 26)
sources.portal_url: AGOL org g26Y0m7OCdjU0ObA (item owner rpierce@cityofsanmateo.org_CityofSanMateo) - no public hub page found
sources.format: ArcGIS REST (Query,Extract; f=geojson supported). Only layer id 26 exists in the service.
sources.vintage: Schema (BASE_ELEV/BUILDING_E/BUILDING_H) matches the county LiDAR footprint product; data last edited 2023-01-20, joined to zoning.

attributes.main_vs_accessory: none (SFE_GARAGE_ZC / SFADU_GARAGE columns exist but null in sample)

sources.name: City of Saratoga - Buildings (2018 ortho outlines, countywide)
sources.format: ArcGIS REST (Query; f=geojson supported). Only layer id 14 exists.
sources.vintage: 'Building outlines from 2018 digital orthophotography project. Countywide' - re-published Aug 2026 (water tanks at Montalvo added).
quirks: No attributes beyond geometry; county 2022 LiDAR layer is newer and adds height - use that, keep this as a cross-check of ortho (wall-ish) vs LiDAR (roof) extents.

sources.name: City of Los Altos - Building_2022LiDAR_Footprints
sources.vintage: 'Data extracted from SANBORN LiDAR remote flight' - the same 2022 countywide Sanborn LiDAR as the county layer.
quirks: Redundant with the county 2022 layer; use county (one client, one host).

sources.name: City of Mountain View - Public/BuildingFootprint
sources.vintage: Per the service's own description (search snippet): a 2D cartographic representation of buildings derived from indirect sources incl. aerial imagery; 'may not reflect current building footprints'.

verified.notes: TCP connect to maps.mountainview.gov:443 timed out (curl, 90 s) and was refused via a second network path (ECONNREFUSED). Likely IP/geo-restricted. Not usable from a cloud host without confirmation.

sources.name: City of San Jose - OPN_OpenDataService building footprints
sources.format: ArcGIS REST MapServer (per catalog; layer id 187 taken from a search-result metadata link and NOT confirmed)
sources.license: City states its GIS data is public domain (work of a local agency under California law), provided 'as is'.
sources.vintage: Building footprints with height/elevation, 'generally from 2006' (OSM import notes); mixed State Plane zone 3 CRS in the shapefile exports.

verified.notes: TCP connect to geo.sanjoseca.gov:443 timed out (curl, 90 s) and was refused via a second path (ECONNREFUSED). Not verified.

quirks: Use the county 2022 LiDAR layer (newer, verified). San Jose's 'rear yard' test needs geometry only.

sources.name: Overture Maps - buildings theme (type=building)
sources.release: 2026-09-23.0 (verified: bucket listing shows part-00000.. ~530 MB zstd parquet files). A 2026-09-23.1 patch exists (GERS id fix for base + building_parts only). Previous: 2026-08-19.0. Overture ships monthly.
sources.format: GeoParquet (WKB geometry, bbox struct columns for predicate pushdown); CLI converts to GeoJSON/GeoJSONSeq/GeoParquet
sources.license: Theme-level ODbL (contains OpenStreetMap). Per attribution page the inputs are: OpenStreetMap (ODbL), Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints (listed as ODbL there), Google Open Buildings (CC BY 4.0), Esri Community Maps (CC BY 4.0), USGS 3DEP for heights. Required attribution: '(c) OpenStreetMap contributors. Available under the Open Database License.'
sources.vintage: Rolling: OSM features carry sources[].update_time (Atherton sample: 2015-11 to 2026-01); MS ML polygons carry no update_time (imagery 2014-2024).

attributes.height: height (m) - present on 24/29 Atherton (OSM) features and 11/11 Lafayette (MS ML, USGS-3DEP-derived) features
attributes.building_type: subtype / class (e.g. residential/house, garage, shed, detached...) - populated only where OSM tags exist: 2/29 at Atherton, 0/11 at Lafayette
attributes.main_vs_accessory: only via class where present; otherwise none
attributes.other: sources[] (dataset, record_id, update_time), has_parts, roof_shape, names, level, is_underground

sources.query_example_cli: pip install overturemaps && overturemaps download --bbox=-122.1988,37.4603,-122.1968,37.4623 -f geojson --type=building -o atherton_buildings.geojson
sources.query_example_duckdb: LOAD spatial; LOAD httpfs; SET s3_region='us-west-2'; SELECT id, subtype, class, height, num_floors, sources[1].dataset AS src, ST_AsText(geometry) FROM read_parquet('s3://overturemaps-us-west-2/release/2026-09-23.0/theme=buildings/type=building/*', filename=true, hive_partitioning=1) WHERE bbox.xmin > -122.1988 AND bbox.xmax < -122.1968 AND bbox.ymin > 37.4603 AND bbox.ymax < 37.4623;
quirks: Conflation rule: where OSM has a building, OSM wins and the MS ML polygon is dropped; elsewhere MS ML (or Google/Esri) fills in. So geometry provenance flips parcel by parcel - read sources[0].dataset.

House + attached garage: OSM mappers in the Peninsula typically trace the whole roof as ONE polygon (house and attached garage merged); detached garages are separate polygons. MS ML polygons are generalized orthogonalized roof blobs and can merge a house with a detached garage/carport when the roofs nearly touch, and can split one house under tree cover.

Not request-time friendly: a bbox scan straight from S3 took ~185 s per query from a laptop (full-partition metadata reads). Pre-extract the six-county bbox (-123.6,36.9,-121.2,38.9) once per release with the CLI or DuckDB into a local GeoParquet/PostGIS table and query that.
Use the .1 patch release path only if you need building_parts/base GERS ids; building geometry is identical.

sources.name: Microsoft GlobalMLBuildingFootprints (2026-08-13 drop)
sources.format: gzip'd newline-delimited GeoJSON features (one per line) per Bing level-9 quadkey; properties: height (m, -1 when unknown), confidence
sources.license: CDLA-Permissive-2.0 per the GitHub README (note: Planetary Computer's ms-buildings STAC collection labels the same data ODbL-1.0 - record both, cite the README).
sources.vintage: Bing imagery 2014-2024; most recent refresh uses Maxar/Vexcel 2020-2025. Drop date 2026-08-13.
sources.query_example: curl -sL 'https://bfppub.z5.web.core.windows.net/2026-08-13/global-buildings.geojsonl/RegionName=UnitedStates/quadkey=023010230/part-00091-110f5303-ff85-4c71-a2bf-c6070024fec8.c000.csv.gz' | gunzip | python3 -c "import sys,json; from shapely.geometry import shape, box; b=box(-122.1988,37.4603,-122.1968,37.4623); print(sum(1 for l in sys.stdin if shape(json.loads(l)['geometry']).intersects(b)))"  # quadkey(lat,lon,9) via Bing tile math

verified.method: manifest downloaded (6.4 MB) + HEAD on the Atherton/Palo Alto tile (Content-Length 95,903,269)
verified.notes: Tile contents not downloaded (92 MB); existence and public access verified. The old host minedbuildings.blob.core.windows.net now returns 409 PublicAccessNotPermitted - do not use URLs from older docs.

quirks: No conflation with OSM: pure ML roof blobs. Adjacent roofs (house + attached garage, or house + nearly-touching detached garage) are frequently merged into one polygon; tree cover can split a house into fragments. ~1% false positives overall.
Whole level-9 tiles (16-92 MB each) must be fetched and filtered locally; 5 tiles cover the six test points, ~6-8 tiles cover the 6-county territory. Cache per tile.
This is the same geometry Overture uses outside OSM-covered areas (e.g. Lafayette), but without Overture's heights from 3DEP unless MS estimated them.

sources.name: Microsoft USBuildingFootprints v2 (legacy, California statewide)
sources.format: GeoJSON (zip, 466 MB; 11,542,912 California polygons; geometry only, optional release/capture-date props)
sources.vintage: ~73 M US footprints from 2019-2020 imagery, remainder ~2012 average; frozen.
sources.query_example: curl -L -o California.geojson.zip https://minedbuildings.z5.web.core.windows.net/legacy/usbuildings-v2/California.geojson.zip  # then clip to the 6-county bbox offline
quirks: Superseded by GlobalML 2026-08-13 for the US; keep only as an offline fallback.

San Jose.note: City host unreachable from here; county layer verified at Palo Alto (same countywide product).

Moraga.note: GAP: no county or city layer.

Orinda.note: GAP: no county or city layer.

Healdsburg.note: No city layer; county layer verified at Healdsburg (33 features).

recommended_registry_extension._comment: Add to each COUNTY_REGISTRY entry in county_registry.py; same keyless /query dialect the parcel client already speaks. primary_pick = how to choose the main house among polygons intersecting the parcel.
